@channel

We are reorganizing the Machine Learning for Theorem Proving stream into a folder "AI and Lean" with several focused streams, to make it easier to find specific topics and improve the signal-to-noise ratio here.

AI and Lean

  • Autoformalization
  • AI authored projects
  • Aristotle
  • Research on ML and Lean (paper discussion only)
  • Prompting, skills, and agent tools
  • Model comparisons for Lean

The channels listed above may be adjusted as we see how they are used, and more may be added if the need arises. If your topic doesn't fit any of the existing streams, it may simply be out of scope for this Zulip.

A few guidelines for all streams in this folder:

  • Stay on topic. These streams are specifically about AI and Lean. "AI for maths" without a Lean focus is off topic.
  • Be concise. Please think carefully before posting, keep threads focused, and avoid posting many times in quick succession.
I have subscribed all subscribers of this channel to all of the new channels. You may want to manually adjust your subscriptions if not all of these are relevant to you.

Please don't start new topics here — use the appropriate new channel instead. If none seems to fit, ask in this topic first.

But remember we are trying to reduce noise here: some topics are simply off-topic for this Zulip entirely.

I welcome the reorganization. The noise was overwhelming the signal at times. :clap:

However, one thing that seems a bit odd is the explicit introduction of Aristotle as a top-level stream while not introducing similar top-level streams for, say, Aristotle competitors and open alternatives. (To be explicit I do not recommend this as a solution as it will lead to too many top-level streams.)

A workable alternative might be to introduce a, say, AI Provers top-level stream and let Aristotle and alternatives live under that?

To add to Kelly’s point it is interesting to think how to organize the three recent projects Leanstral, OpenGauss, and the new Aristotle. The dominant paradigm now is some sort of agentic framework which is a combination of Model+Scaffold. Leanstral is more technically Leanstral model with Vibe scaffold. Claude code is technically Claude Opus/Sonnet models with Claude Code (plus optionally Lean MCP and Lean Skills) scaffold. OpenGauss is technically the OpenGuass scaffold around Claude Opus (but you could swap the model with say Leanstral). Aristotle is similar (even if the model/scaffold details are secret).

And to add to that, the distinction between proving and autoformalizing is going away. All the above tools I just mentioned do both proving and autoformalization. The FormalQualBench “autoformalization” benchmark is just a proving benchmark the same as PutnamBench. The only difference is that the theorems are wellknown (and if the agent uses internet that is a good thing and not a bad thing).

As to what to name things, that is famously one of the two hard problems, so I don’t have a clean answer but just wanted to offer that perspective.

If in the future there are other Lean-specific AIs which

  • are as capable/useful as Aristotle is today
  • have interest from both users and authors in having a stream

then I think we should add more streams, and if (oh happy day) there become too many satisfying those conditions, we can move them to another folder.

I was trying to be subtle. But I'll be a bit less subtle now. Sorry beforehand.

Participants in this forum, broadly speaking, should choose winners and losers, not myself or forum admins.

If admins pick such winners, or even seem to be picking such winners (which seems to be happening here), then it will sew distrust in the forum and serve to fracture instead of unifying it, and fostering this forum and this community is a goal I think we all have in common.

Again sorry for being less subtle, but I think this is an important point.

I think I agree with @Kelly Davis and was also startled at first why Aristotle is such a top tier channel here. I don't mind the Aristotle team and I have personally tried Aristotle for a while now (with quite some mixed results) but I don't understand why not simply add a channel like "AI Provers" and something less branded. We all welcome more progress of neural autoprovers if the pool of such increases (oh happy day indeed) and a good way to do so is to provide a general folder where they can all grow with equal inclusivity.
Could I share some ideas proved by AI here?
@Fei GAO probably #AI authored projects is a better place. If Lean is involved. If the ideas proved by AI are informal texts, then it's off-topic for this Zulip.
